5e Spell Maker: Desktop launcher for a local mirror of a browser tool that formats homebrew D&D 5e spells like sourcebook entries and exports them as images. A preservation mirror of a third-party itch.io tool so it keeps working if the original page goes down, wrapped as a local app. Writing a homebrew spell for a campaign; exporting a spell card image; handing a player a formatted spell.
5eTools: App launcher that starts a local web server on port 5050 for the 5eTools D&D reference site stored in Google Drive and opens it in the browser. Appears to be a one-click way to run the self-hosted 5etools reference offline for D&D prep. Looking up spells, monsters and items during game prep; testing homebrew data locally; opening the reference without terminal steps.
actual-gameplay replay + audit: Two Python scripts that drive the Actual Gameplay iPhone app in the simulator: replay.py plays each level's stored solution, audit.py stress-tests levels and prints TRIVIAL, FRAGILE or BROKEN verdicts. Appears to exist so puzzle levels can be regression-tested and difficulty-checked automatically instead of by hand-playing each one after every change. After editing level data or game physics; before shipping a new level; checking whether a level can be solved by sloppy input.
add-reminder: Wrapper around a Swift EventKit helper that creates Apple Reminders with due dates and repeat rules, rebuilding the binary when the source changes. Built because AppleScript cannot set recurrence on Reminders, so repeating reminders needed EventKit. Creating a one-off or repeating Apple Reminder from a script; scheduling a daily or weekly nudge; any reminder needing a due time or recurrence.
ai-bill-scan: Python script that scans govinfo BILLSTATUS bulk zips for a whole Congress and emits JSON of every AI-related bill plus a per-member sponsor and cosponsor index with party and date. Built to answer questions like which members of a party have signed AI-risk legislation from primary-source signatures instead of recalled or scraped lists, without an API key or rate limit. Whip counts on AI legislation by party; checking who sponsored or cosponsored a given class of AI bill; refreshing the data after a new Congress zip is published; prepping advocacy or office-outreach research.
alarm-triage: Stdlib Python script summarizing guard-hook denials and notification banners over a time window, grouped by rule and title, with repeat offenders. Built because nothing read back the harness's alarm streams, so recurring false alarms and noisy watchers went unnoticed. Weekly review of harness alarms; finding which rule or watcher to fix; investigating a burst of banners.
alltrails: A command-line tool for AllTrails that searches trails by name, prints trail stats and descriptions, lists recent reviews with their dates and reported conditions, writes the route as a GPX track, and shows the 7-day trailhead forecast. It also uploads GPX files to the user's own account as shareable custom routes, one map segment for each GPX track, and deletes them again. It was built on 2026-10-06 while planning a backpacking trip, because AllTrails blocks plain HTTP requests and its MCP server has no reviews, route geometry or write tools. Use it to compare candidate trails, to check recent conditions such as mud, flooding or ticks, to load a trail route into a GPS app, or to turn a planned multi-day route into a link that a hiking group can open on their phones.
ami-play: Unofficial Python CLI for the AMI Play jukebox app that finds bars, reads live queues and pricing, searches the catalog, and queues songs. Built to control bar jukeboxes from the terminal and let MIST see or queue music without the phone app. Checking what is playing at a bar; searching a song; queueing a track; managing favorites or playlists.
analyze-leaf: Offline analyzer for a WaveLynx LEAF MIFARE DESFire NFC dump that tests whether a candidate master key reproduces the card's free-read CMAC signature. Built as the verification instrument for the challenge of obtaining a LEAF keyset for the apartment fob project, since a candidate key can be checked without the card or reader present. Testing a guessed master key against a fob dump; validating the diversification math with --selftest; confirming a keyset before deriving per-app keys from a UID.
Animal Kill Clock: macOS desktop widget showing a live running count of animals killed for food so far this year, styled after the U.S. Animal Kill Clock website. Built to keep that statistic visible on the desktop as an ambient reminder. Launching the widget after login or a crash; checking the current year-to-date count.
Anna's Archive: Local Flask app in a native window that finds the current working Anna's Archive domain from several feeds, verifies it, and scaffolds member features. Built because the site rotates domains as they get seized, so an always-current entry point saves hunting for the live address. Opening Anna's Archive without knowing the current domain; searching for a book; extending the membership download features.
app-shell build-app: Shell script that builds a native /Applications .app wrapping a localhost web app in a WKWebView window, using a shared Python venv and a launchd kickstart. Built so local web apps get a real Dock icon, menu-bar name and their own TCC identity instead of living in a browser tab. Used by The Priory and Trawl. Turning a new localhost web app into a double-clickable app; rebuilding a wrapper after changing its URL, icon or launchd label; fixing a wrapper's permissions identity.
arctic-shift-scan: Python scanner that pulls every post from a subreddit over the last N days via the Arctic Shift archive API, plus megathread comment trees, into a JSON snapshot. Reddit's unauthenticated JSON endpoints are blocked, so this reads a public archive without Reddit credentials to feed the local events skill with Kansas City posts. Weekly local-events discovery; checking what a city subreddit is discussing; any job needing bulk Reddit post history without an API key.
audiotee: A macOS command-line tool that captures the audio output of chosen processes, or of the whole system, through Apple's Core Audio process taps (macOS 14.2 or later) and writes raw PCM chunks to standard output. It was adopted to feed the govee-music light sync daemon with Pocket Bard's audio without a virtual audio device and without muting the speakers. Use it to analyze what an app is playing in real time, to record one app's audio to a file, to feed a transcription or beat detector from system audio, or to mute one app while sampling it.
avatar-fit: Python script that fits an image's minimum enclosing circle to a circular avatar crop and verifies that no opaque pixel falls outside it. Built after logos shipped clipped in circular profile croppers such as ESPN Fantasy, where padding to a square was not enough. Preparing a profile picture for a circular cropper; checking whether a logo will clip; setting a background color and size.
Bestagon: Local Flask web app on port 5019 for managing hex-grid combat encounters, loading JSON maps with 5 ft flat-top hexes. Made as a tabletop battle-map manager for Alex's campaigns; the name is a pun on hexagons being the bestagons. Running or prepping a combat encounter on a hex map; adding a new map JSON to the maps folder; testing a hex-grid rule.
bg3wiki-mcp: Gives Claude Code sessions search, page reading and structured Cargo queries against bg3.wiki, the Baldur's Gate 3 community wiki, through ProfessionalWiki's MediaWiki MCP server. Adopted instead of building a wiki scraper when Alex and MIST started playing BG3 split screen. Use it to look up a spell, item, class feature, quest step or character mid-game, or to query the wiki's data tables for builds and loot.
Bookmarklets page: Static local HTML page of draggable javascript: bookmarklets, such as Wayback Machine snapshot and Save Page Now, defined in a single BM object. Appears to have been built to keep browser bookmarklets in one version-controlled place instead of hand-made bookmarks. Adding a new bookmarklet; dragging the set into a fresh browser; archiving the current page to the Wayback Machine.
cad: Command-line 3D printing toolkit: builds a part from a build123d Python script, an OpenSCAD file, or a signed-distance-field mesh script, exports STL, STEP and 3MF, runs a printability report (watertight, bodies, bed fit, overhang share, mass), repairs broken meshes with pymeshfix, renders preview sheets and close-ups with f3d, converts mesh formats, slices with PrusaSlicer for print time, filament and stability warnings, and makes Blender studio renders in clay or vertex colour. Built in October 2026 so MIST can design printable parts in code and show them in the Console's inline 3D viewer instead of using a GUI CAD app. Use it to design a bracket, clip, case or holder to measured dimensions; to turn a picture into a printable replica; to check whether a downloaded STL will print; to show Alex a polished render of a part before he prints it.
cad-setup: Installer for the 3D printing toolkit: creates the Python 3.12 venv with build123d, trimesh, manifold3d and pymeshfix, installs OpenSCAD snapshot, PrusaSlicer and f3d through Homebrew, and clones or updates the BOSL2 OpenSCAD library. Exists so the cad CLI can be rebuilt on a fresh machine or after a broken brew upgrade in one step. Use it when cad reports a missing venv, when BOSL2 needs updating, or when setting up the toolkit on another Mac.
chat-draft: Python CLI managing fantasy league chat reply drafts: save, list, show, send, skip, with a check that refuses to send into a moved-on thread. Built after 2026-09-20 so chat replies are never sent unattended, and a human approves each reply. Saving or reviewing a draft; sending an approved reply; skipping one; overriding the stale-thread check.
chat-watch: Python watcher run every 10 minutes that finds unanswered ESPN Fantasy Chat threads and has a headless Claude decide whether to reply, keyed by message ID. Built to keep league chat answered promptly while ensuring direct messages go to Alex rather than getting an unattended reply. Debugging a missed or double reply; running with --dry-run; adjusting the daily reply cap; checking how direct messages are handed off.
check_boundaries.py: AST-based checker that fails when a script in one top-level harness directory imports another directory's internals or adds a sibling directory to sys.path. Written because the harness is a set of independent hyphenated scripts that import-linter cannot model, and cross-tool coupling needed to be caught automatically after each edit. Runs automatically in the post-edit quality-gate hook; run it by hand across the whole repo before a large refactor; add a blessed cross-island import to its allow list when a deliberate shared interface is needed.
Chromatic Set: Local Flask app on port 5018 that reads every pixel of an uploaded image and turns color into pitch-class sets to compose a roughly two-minute piece. Appears to have been built to explore mapping the hue wheel onto the twelve-tone chromatic circle, using real Forte set theory to read an image as music. Turning a picture into a composition; demonstrating pitch-class set theory; experimenting with color-to-pitch mappings.
Claude Animation (song-sync): Fork of a p5.js and p5.brush watercolour animation kit whose song-sync command detects tempo and lyric cue times from a song so frames render in sync. Built to make hand-painted animated videos and music videos in code, locking visuals to a generated song instead of timing beats by hand. Making a music video for a generated track; rendering a short Clawd or cartoon clip; syncing lyric cues to a song with a known BPM.
Claude Home: Desktop app launching a live dashboard for home devices: electricity usage, HVAC, bedroom air quality, and the Nest doorbell, with bundled integrations that pull the data. Consolidates several home data sources into one viewer. It grew from an energy dashboard into a general home hub. Checking power usage or HVAC runtime at a glance; watching bedroom CO2; opening the doorbell feed.
claude-spend: Estimates what local Claude Code usage would cost at API rates by scanning session transcripts, deduplicating messages and pricing tokens per model per month. Built to see the API-equivalent cost of Claude Code use, since one response is logged once per content block and needs deduping to count correctly. Checking monthly spend; comparing model cost; updating rates when pricing changes.
claude-stable-path: Bash script that pins the auto-updating claude CLI to one unchanging path so macOS TCC permissions, especially Full Disk Access, survive each release. Each CLI release lands at a new versioned path and TCC keys grants by path, so grants died roughly daily. This fixes that at the path level. Re-running after a CLI update breaks file access; checking that the stable path still resolves; debugging Full Disk Access loss for headless Claude runs.
Clippy Meme: Native app shell around the local paperclip meme generator served on port 5031 by launchd, wrapped in the shared app-shell WKWebView. Built so the Clippy-style meme generator opens as a normal Mac app instead of a browser page. Making a Clippy meme image; exporting a PNG from the generator; checking the paperclip-meme launchd service is up.
com.alexhedtke.dubpace: Daily launchd job that runs dubpace-update.sh to fetch new One Pace dub episodes from Pixeldrain, rename them to Plex format, place them in season folders, and trigger a Plex scan. Created to keep the self-hosted dub library current without manual downloads, resuming across runs because Pixeldrain rate-limits. Checking why new dub episodes are missing; running a backfill by hand; diagnosing a failure when the external SSD is unreachable.
com.alexhedtke.dubsubs: Hourly job that runs subgen.sh to transcribe One Pace dub episodes with whisper.cpp large-v3, post-correct them with a glossary, and write English sidecar subtitles for Plex. Built to give the self-hosted dub library subtitles without paying for a service, using cached raw transcripts so glossary changes are cheap to reapply. Adding subtitles to newly downloaded dub episodes; fixing a recurring mistranscription; checking batch progress by season.
com.alexhedtke.passage: KeepAlive launchd job serving Passage, a Flask paywall remover with rail-race fetching, reader mode, a freeze cache, and a library of cleaned pages. Keeps the paywall reader always available at a local port so any article link can be opened cleanly. Reading a paywalled article; checking that the Passage server is up; opening the library of cleaned pages.
com.alexhedtke.plex: launchd job that runs Plex Media Server through plex-guard.sh only while the external media drive is mounted, at login and on every volume mount. Built so Plex does not start against a missing library when the media SSD is unplugged, and starts itself when it is plugged in. Debugging why Plex is not running; changing which drive it depends on; understanding the mount-triggered start.
com.exobrain.5etools-server: Launchd job that keeps a local 5etools D&D reference site running by executing npm run serve:dev in the 5etools folder at load. Appears to have been set up so the self-hosted 5etools data and homebrew are always available offline for D&D work. Looking up spells, monsters, or items during play; testing homebrew content; restarting the server after an update.
com.exobrain.airdrop-console: Every-15-minute launchd job running a Python watcher that picks up things AirDropped to the Mac and delivers them to a MIST Console chat. Appears to exist so photos and files sent from the phone reach MIST without opening a chat manually. Debugging an AirDrop that never showed up in the console; adjusting the polling interval; checking whether the watcher is running.
com.exobrain.appliances-poll: Every five minutes polls LG ThinQ appliance state and writes appliances-data.json for the Claude Home dashboard panel. Appears to have been built so the home dashboard can show washer and dryer state from the official ThinQ API, following the Evergy and Nest pattern of one writer and a read-only app. Debugging a stale Appliances panel; adding another appliance brand; checking cycle status from data.
com.exobrain.asp-baton-watch: Every-6-hour launchd job that polls retailer product pages for one specific tactical baton model and alerts Alex on Discord when a price falls below a threshold. Built to catch a price drop on one exact SKU without checking stores manually, after an audit found some target pages served the wrong model. Checking the watcher is alive; adjusting the alert price; adding a retailer URL pinned to the exact SKU.
com.exobrain.auto-commit-harness: Nightly shell job that commits and pushes pending changes in the harness repo after a conservative filename-based gitignore check for secrets, runtime state and large binaries. Replaced a Claude routine that spent a full headless Opus session to do what a shell script can do; it is the mechanical backstop for auto-commit. Checking why changes were or were not committed overnight; adjusting the auto-ignore patterns; confirming the safety net ran.
com.exobrain.awair-co2-watcher: Every 5 minutes it polls an Awair Element over the local API, logs CO2 and humidity to a CSV, and alerts by banner and Discord DM during active hours. Built to capture overnight air quality in the bedroom and warn when CO2 gets high, without middle-of-the-night notifications. Charting bedroom air quality; checking whether ventilation is adequate; debugging missing alerts or a gap in air-log.csv.
com.exobrain.awair-rollup: Nightly job running awair-rollup.py, which turns the CO2 and humidity time-series CSV into a daily Air Quality Log note in the Obsidian vault. Built to make raw Awair sensor readings into a readable per-day record, following the same pattern as the Energy Log. Checking daily CO2 or humidity trends; rebuilding the air quality note; diagnosing a night with no rollup.
com.exobrain.backup: Daily 02:00 job that builds one collective tarball of the harness, the Obsidian vault and every repo's gitignored files, uploads it to Google Drive, and prunes with grandfather-father-son retention. GitHub holds code but not secrets, databases or the vault, so this creates one atomic restore point for everything else. Restoring after data loss; verifying last night's backup ran; changing retention; checking that a new gitignored file is covered.
com.exobrain.backup-resume: Every-30-minute launchd job that runs backup-exobrain.sh to build one tarball of the harness, the vault, and gitignored repo data, upload it to Drive, and prune by retention. Created as a single atomic restore point for everything GitHub does not hold; the frequent schedule lets an interrupted or slept run resume. Verifying the latest backup exists; restoring after data loss; changing retention or what the archive contains.
com.exobrain.bodyguard-weekly: Daily launchd job running the bodyguard weekly script, which refreshes breach data and builds a passive OSINT query plan, then posts a notification to review it. Built to keep a recurring check on Alex's public exposure, such as breaches and data brokers, without remembering to run scans. Reviewing the weekly exposure scan; checking the latest plan file in the logs; updating the security log after a scan.
com.exobrain.bounty-hunter: Every-10-minute Python watcher that polls an allowlist of vetted open-source bounty payers for fresh bounties so Alex can be first to respond. Built after recon showed public bounty boards are either honeypot farms or swarmed by bots within hours, so speed on known-good payers is the only edge. Tuning the allowed orgs; checking whether a bounty alert was missed; the github skill's bounty lane.
com.exobrain.chat-watch: Every 10 minutes it checks ESPN Fantasy Chat for unanswered league threads and runs a headless Claude to reply, while direct messages are handed to Alex instead. Appears to exist so the fantasy league chat gets timely replies from MIST while private conversations stay with Alex. Debugging a missed or duplicate league chat reply; changing the daily reply cap; checking the log for a run that answered nothing.
com.exobrain.claude-bot: Always-on launchd job running the MIST Discord bot, a discord.py client with a command registry, SQLite storage, and pluggable modules. Built to give a few private Discord servers a MIST assistant, modeled on the open-source Fletcher bot without its cross-server machinery. Restarting the bot after a code change; checking why it is offline; adding a feature module or command.
com.exobrain.claude-cli-update: Launchd job running claude-cli-autoupdate.sh four times daily to update the Claude Code CLI and notify Alex when the version changes. Created because the Console discovers models by reading the claude binary, so a stale CLI is the only reason a new model would fail to appear. When a new model is missing from the picker; after an update breaks a hardcoded path; adjusting update frequency.
com.exobrain.claude-stable-path: Job that pins the Claude Code CLI to one unchanging path whenever a new version lands, so macOS TCC permissions keyed by path survive updates. The CLI updates about daily to a new versioned path, which orphaned its Full Disk Access and other grants and caused a flood of permission prompts. Investigating recurring permission dialogs after a Claude update; checking the stable symlink; debugging launchd jobs that call claude.
com.exobrain.comp-hunter: Every-6-hour launchd job polling Zindi, Apart Research sprints, Kaggle, and DrivenData for prize competitions and alerting on winnable ones. Second pipeline in the money portfolio: chase pre-funded competitions an agent can work on, with AI-safety sprints flagged for Alex's background. Reviewing new competitions; tuning the minimum prize or deadline filter; adding a competition source.
com.exobrain.cowork-sync: Five-minute launchd job running cowork-sync, which keeps the harness CLAUDE.md and the iCloud Claude Cowork copy identical in both directions by hash. Built because iCloud stores symlinks as tiny objects, so the cloud side must be a real file that is kept in step with the canonical one. Editing CLAUDE.md and needing the Cowork copy updated; diagnosing a sync conflict where both sides changed; running with --status.
com.exobrain.day-zero-watch: Every 30 minutes it snapshots a Facebook page counting down 3000 days, archiving text and screenshots and alerting on the countdown ending, a new payload post, or the page vanishing. Built to preserve whatever the page posted at zero in case it was deleted, with alerts as a secondary function. Reviewing the archive after the countdown ended; reusing the pattern to archive another page likely to disappear.
com.exobrain.deathcafe-kc-watch: Job polling a local Death Cafe host's event profile every 12 hours and alerting Alex on Discord when a new event id appears. Built so Alex learns the moment the next monthly session is scheduled, since dates post only weeks ahead. Confirming the watcher still runs; adapting the pattern to another event listing; checking which dates it has seen.
com.exobrain.dhs-ia-watch: Launchd job running a headless Claude that finds the newest teleconference invite in Gmail and writes the fresh Teams link and passcode into that calendar event. Built because the agency issues a new meeting link for every biweekly call with no recurring invite, making a bare calendar hold useless. Missing connection details on the call day; changing the search window or run times; reusing the pattern for another meeting series with rotating links.
com.exobrain.diesel-bike-watch: Twelve-hourly watcher that polls motorcycle listing sites for diesel motorcycles and alerts on any listing ID it has not seen before. Roughly one diesel motorcycle is on the market worldwide at a time, so there is no fixed product URL to price and discovery of new listings is the goal. Adding a listing source; checking the seen-listing state; debugging why an alert did or did not fire.
com.exobrain.discord-digest: Every-4-hour launchd job that waits for network and runs the Discord digest fetch of the friend group server for the briefing to summarize. Feeds the daily briefing's Discord section so plans and events from friends are not missed. Debugging a stale digest; checking the fetch logs; changing the digest cadence.
com.exobrain.eject-assist: Always-running launchd job that watches diskarbitrationd for failed volume ejects and frees the busy volume by asking what holds it to quit, then ejects. Built so clicking eject on an external drive works even when background processes hold it open. It never forces an unmount or kills a process; a holder that will not quit leaves the volume mounted and is named in the notification. Ejecting the Extreme SSD or another external volume; investigating what blocks an eject; running disk_eject.py free manually.
com.exobrain.energy-pull: Daily 06:30 job that waits for network, pulls Evergy electricity usage, then loads Evergy and Nest data into the energy.db warehouse. Built so cost, per-floor HVAC runtime and weather history stay joinable and current, after early pulls were lost when the Mac woke without Wi-Fi. Analyzing power bill drivers; checking whether yesterday's usage landed; debugging a missed pull in the energy log.
com.exobrain.envelope-budget-sync: Launchd job running sync_cli.py four times daily, the same sync as the envelope budget app's Refresh button, without the web server. Built so budget data stays current without Alex opening the app. Diagnosing stale budget numbers; checking sync results before a money question; changing how often it refreshes.
com.exobrain.fitbit-token: Launchd job running token-check.mjs four times daily to exercise the Fitbit OAuth token through the MCP server's own refresh path and raise a notification if re-auth is needed. Made so a broken refresh chain surfaces as a banner rather than a dark health pipeline discovered during the morning briefing. Health pulls fail with auth errors; checking whether the Fitbit token is warm; triggering the reauth flow.
com.exobrain.framesdirect-return-watch: Hourly launchd watcher that reads the local Gmail mirror Maildir for new mail about one online order return and raises a banner when any arrives. Built because the retailer's return status page needs a login and the carrier tracking page blocks scripted access, so the order and refund emails are the only readable signal. Use it to follow a return or refund to completion, as a template for any watcher keyed on incoming mail, or to check whether a retailer has confirmed receipt.
com.exobrain.gatorade-watch: Three-hourly watcher that polls retailer pages for a specific Gatorade flavor and sends a Discord message when one flips from sold out to buyable. Built because the product is often sold out and checking retailer pages by hand is tedious. Adding another retailer; investigating a missed restock; using it as a template for another stock watcher.
com.exobrain.gmail-mirror: Hourly launchd job that runs mbsync to pull the whole Gmail account (All Mail) into a local Maildir, then copies that Maildir to the external SSD when it is mounted. Built as a hedge against an unexplained Google account lockout, when Gmail had no copy anywhere outside Google. The mirror is append-only: server deletions never remove local mail. Use it to read old mail offline, to restore mail after losing the account, to grep years of email locally, or as the pattern for mirroring another IMAP account.
com.exobrain.haircut-check: Daily 10:00 launchd job that checks whether a haircut is due every six weeks and, if so, launches a headless MIST run to book a slot around the calendar. Replaced an earlier booking-app version with a single-salon flow, so the haircut gets booked without Alex remembering or shopping for slots. Checking why a cut was or was not booked; adjusting the interval; debugging the booking token re-mint.
com.exobrain.headless-chrome-reaper: Two-minute shell job that kills only genuinely stuck headless Chrome render processes and their hung wrappers, gated on several signals so active renders survive. Built because headless Chrome dump-dom and screenshot calls can hang forever on macOS and pile up. Chrome processes eating memory; tuning the stuck thresholds; confirming concurrent renders in other sessions are safe.
com.exobrain.heartbeat-check: Daily 10:15 script that checks whether the day's routines produced their expected outputs and raises one banner listing anything missing or stale, with no model call. Replaced an older scheduled task; jobs that never ran say nothing themselves, so this checks outputs instead. Adding a check for a new routine; confirming morning jobs ran after the Mac slept; running with --dry-run to see verdicts.
com.exobrain.heilung-tour-watch: Job polling a Bandsintown-fed static mirror for tour dates and the band's RSS feed every 6 hours, alerting Alex on Discord. Built so Alex hears of a new tour announcement immediately, since the band posts mainly on social media that scripts cannot poll. Checking whether new tour dates appeared; copying the two-source pattern for another artist; fixing a false alert.
com.exobrain.imessage-sync: Every-15-minute launchd job running imessage-sync.py under a stable interpreter with Full Disk Access to snapshot the Messages database and contacts map into a cache. Created because Full Disk Access is granted per binary path and Claude Code's versioned path broke the grant on every update. iMessage searches return stale results; the Full Disk Access grant needs rebuilding; changing sync frequency.
com.exobrain.inbox-server: Launchd agent that keeps the Inbox clone's Flask server running on 127.0.0.1:5008 with KeepAlive, so the clone opens in any browser without the native window. Made so a plain browser bookmark to the clone always works, and so the snooze scheduler runs when the desktop app is closed. Use it when the Inbox bookmark does not load, when snoozed mail does not return, or when the desktop window and the browser must share one server.
com.exobrain.job-listings-sync: Job, run every five minutes and on file changes, that runs reconcile.py to keep job-listing note frontmatter consistent in the Obsidian Job Listings folder. Appears to have been built so listing status fields stay consistent after edits without doing manual frontmatter cleanup. Debugging a listing whose status did not update; changing the reconcile rules; checking that the sync is running.
com.exobrain.job-scan: Daily 09:00 launchd job running the headless job-search discovery scan across email alerts, scripted boards, LinkedIn, and other lanes, filtered by hard gates and deduped. Automates daily job discovery during a job search, replacing manual board checking, and notifies only on new verified candidates. Investigating a missed or empty scan day; checking new listing notes; changing a gate or lane.
com.exobrain.kcurbex-watch: Twelve-hour launchd job that runs an unattended pass over the KC Urbex forum, pacing requests gently because the board is a small volunteer site. Built so new site reports and meetups from the forum reach Alex without manual checking. Reviewing the latest urbex pass; checking why a report or meetup was missed; not raising the request rate.
com.exobrain.lineup-watch: Every 15 minutes it checks the fantasy lineup for OUT, IR, bye, empty or questionable starters before lock and notifies, with --fix making verified swaps for definite problems. Built so a fantasy lineup problem gets caught and repaired before kickoff without Alex checking manually. Debugging a missed lineup ping or unexpected swap; adjusting the ping window; checking that the Mac stays awake before a lock.
com.exobrain.loki-poll: Hourly job polling the PetKit cloud for the litterbox and logging the cat's per-visit weight, time, and duration, plus a daily Obsidian note. Built because litterbox frequency and weight drift are early warnings of cat health problems, ahead of visible symptoms. Checking the cat's weight trend; investigating an unusual visit pattern; re-running discovery after the PetKit API changes.
com.exobrain.mem-watchdog: Always-on launchd daemon that logs top processes by memory, warns at a threshold, and kills sustained runaway processes, with a fast lane for memory-hungry search tools. Built after runaway apps and a grep regex blowup exhausted the 8GB Mac's RAM and froze it, leaving no record of the culprit. Investigating a freeze or slowdown; reading which process was killed and why; changing warn or kill thresholds or the protected list.
com.exobrain.missing-person-candidate-ra: Daily job that runs mp-rate for the past seven days and notifies with how often the missing-person news-candidate track fires. The candidate threshold was set from one cold-start sample, so this measures the steady-state firing rate to check whether the threshold is right. Reviewing whether the two-agreement threshold needs tuning; checking watcher health; looking at candidate volume over time.
com.exobrain.missing-person-watch: Daily 08:15 launchd job running the missing-person toolkit's watch command for one specific case to check databases and news. Automates daily monitoring of the sources that would change first if the person were found or new information appeared. Checking that the daily case watch ran; reviewing the latest watch output; pausing it when the case closes.
com.exobrain.mist-console-autocommit: Thirty-minute shell job that commits and pushes the private MIST Console repo, including conversation history, and does nothing when the tree is clean. Built so Console chat data and local edits stay synced without manual commits. Confirming Console changes reached the remote; debugging a failed push; adding paths that should not be committed.
com.exobrain.mist-console-watch: Every minute it checks that the MIST Console answers on port 5014 and reopens the app through LaunchServices if not. Built so the Console recovers after a crash, quit or login and the phone can reach the Mac whenever it is on. Mid-draft or right after a draft to rank all rosters; printing top rosters with --rosters N to learn from them; run before leaving the draft room.
fantasy draft simulator: Offline Python simulator that runs a 13-seat fantasy draft against ESPN auto-bot or crowd-ADP opponents and grades optimal starting lineups on ESPN projections. fantasy draft supervisor: Python supervisor that owns the draft driver's command channel during a live fantasy draft, logging each pick to supervise.log and driving a progress bar from roster count. fantasy season_sim: Python script that scores two draft boards (our value-over-replacement board versus ESPN projections) and runs a Monte Carlo of the season on the real schedule with confidence intervals. ff: Read-only ESPN fantasy football CLI that reads the league through the ESPN v3 API using stored session cookies and surfaces the numbers the playbook uses. Checking rosters, standings or matchups; gathering data for start/sit, waivers or trades; preparing weekly decisions.
fitbit-mcp: Launcher for the forked Fitbit MCP server, which loads secrets from the harness environment and runs the compiled Node server over stdio. fitbit-token-check: Shell entry point that runs the Fitbit MCP token health check under Node. Health data pulls failing; checking token expiry manually; before a large Fitbit backfill.

gen_art.py: Python script that generates card art for every entry in the tarot deck's deck.json using mist-image, skipping existing files and reporting progress to the console. gridpoint-build-install: Shell script that regenerates the Xcode project, does a clean signed Release build of the Gridpoint weather app, prints profile expiry, and installs it wirelessly to the paired iPhone. gridpoint-monitor: Python script that logs NWS and Open-Meteo forecasts plus observed KMKC weather into SQLite every 30 minutes, with score.py reporting per-source accuracy. hand-letter: uv script that draws text as pen strokes using Hershey stroke fonts with per-letter wobble, tilt, pressure and felt-tip texture, saved as a transparent PNG or over a base image. harness-commit: Bash script that stages, privacy-audits, injection-scans, commits, and pushes the public harness repo, with a dry-run mode. Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone: Native Apple Silicon build of the 2001 PC game using a patched SurrealEngine (Unreal Engine 1 reimplementation) rendered through Vulkan and MoltenVK, with notes and scripts. ig: Read-only Instagram CLI that borrows the logged-in Chrome session to list an account's posts and scan tracked accounts into a JSON file, with pacing and a cooldown after a 429. league-scan: Python script that measures each fantasy manager's engagement from ESPN records: zero-score starters, bench points left, moves, and trade offer outcomes. letter-pdf: Python script that renders a plain-markdown letter into a formal print-ready PDF with letterhead, headers, and running page footers in the house style. lineup-watch: Python watcher run every fifteen minutes that checks the fantasy lineup for problems before kickoff locks, notifies only on real issues, and with --fix repairs definite ones. linkedin-mcp: Shell wrapper that launches mcp-server-linkedin with macOS hidden-target mode disabled so the browser runs in real headless mode. Starting the LinkedIn MCP server; diagnosing bogus sign-in prompts; patching the server after an update.
loopkit: A Python engine for music that repeats with no seam. Syncing new events after creating them on Luma; publishing drafts; checking for cancelled events still live on Meetup.

Visualizing a homebrew world map as a planet; exporting a rotating GIF or screenshot; adding rings and moons to a planet.
matter: A non-interactive wrapper around the matter.js controller shell that makes this computer a Matter admin on the home network. Finding events near Kansas City; reading an event's details; RSVPing; scanning a group's upcoming events.
memory-index-check: A read-only lint for MIST's persistent memory index.
